stories.title: Schools are catching on to Big Tech’s playbook
stories.simple_summary: AI companies are giving free training materials and lessons to schools to teach students about AI. Schools are accepting these offers because they want students to learn the technology.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have kids or grandkids in school, they'll likely be learning AI tools. It's worth asking their schools who's teaching the material and whether it's balanced, since the companies providing the lessons benefit if more people use their products.

stories.title: Anthropic reveals rogue AI agents hate CAPTCHAs, just like you
stories.simple_summary: Researchers found that AI programs struggle with CAPTCHAs—those puzzles websites use to prove you're human, not a robot.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to computer engineers and security researchers—nothing you need to worry about in your daily life.

stories.title: India’s Pocket FM doubles revenue run rate to $500M as AI powers 93% of audio content
stories.simple_summary: An Indian company called Pocket FM now uses AI to create almost all of its audio stories, which made their production costs about 80 times cheaper.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows how AI is making entertainment cheaper to produce, which could eventually mean more affordable audio content, though many voice actors and writers may lose work.

stories.title: Universal Music is launching an AI music platform with ElevenLabs
stories.simple_summary: Universal Music Group is creating a tool where people can use famous songs to make remixes and new versions, powered by AI.
stories.why_it_matters: Music fans might enjoy remixing songs, but musicians and songwriters should know this uses their work—it's worth understanding what permissions and payments are involved.

stories.title: Meta’s Muse AI works and creeps me out
stories.simple_summary: Meta released a new AI assistant called Muse that can help with shopping, emails, and trip planning by doing tasks for you online.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Facebook or Instagram, you may eventually see this tool available to help with everyday online chores, though like any AI, it may make mistakes.

stories.title: AI agents are flooding public services with new requests
stories.simple_summary: AI programs are submitting many requests to government services and benefit programs, and researchers are studying whether this is causing problems.
stories.why_it_matters: This is still early research—it mostly matters to government agencies right now, though it suggests AI is already interacting with public services in ways we're still figuring out.

stories.title: Maven Robotics wants to steal your robot deployment deal
stories.simple_summary: A robotics company called Maven Robotics just raised $100 million and is ready to sell robots to businesses that need to automate tasks.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and large companies looking to use robots—nothing you need to act on unless you're in manufacturing or logistics.

stories.title: Why the current tech backlash feels different
stories.simple_summary: This headline points to a longer discussion about why people are now feeling frustrated or skeptical about big tech companies in a new way.
stories.why_it_matters: This is an opinion piece rather than news about a specific AI development—it's worth reading if you're curious about why tech criticism is growing, but there's no specific action to take.

stories.title: Mathematicians want proof OpenAI didn’t use their work
stories.simple_summary: Mathematicians are accusing OpenAI of using their unpublished research to train its AI without permission or credit.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a legal and ethical issue being worked out between researchers and AI companies—for now, it's mostly a concern for the math and AI communities, though it touches on larger questions about who owns ideas.

stories.title: AI research startup Listen Labs scrubbed a $1.5B funding round for Salesforce talks
stories.simple_summary: A startup called Listen Labs cancelled a large funding deal to instead have talks with Salesforce about being acquired.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech industry watchers—nothing affecting ordinary people.

stories.title: OpenAI adds a prominent AI doomer to its board of directors
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI hired a well-known AI researcher named Paul Christiano who has worried publicly about AI safety risks.
stories.why_it_matters: This suggests OpenAI is trying to listen to critics about AI safety, which is good, though it's mostly a signal to investors and AI watchers rather than affecting your daily life.

stories.title: Massachusetts hits data centers with new clean power rules
stories.simple_summary: Massachusetts passed new rules requiring data centers (the huge warehouses that store and run AI and cloud services) to use clean energy.
stories.why_it_matters: If you live in Massachusetts or nearby, this means data centers will use less fossil fuel, which is good for the environment—and it may inspire other states to do the same.
